title: One auth retry, triggered by the substring auth in the RPC error message
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:134-140 - `do { session = try await openSession(connection) } catch let error as RPCError where error.message.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("auth") && !authMethods.isEmpty { _ = try await connection.request("authenticate", ["methodId": .string(authMethods[0])]); session = try await openSession(connection) }`
preconditions: The first openSession threw an RPCError whose message contains "auth" case-insensitively, and authMethods is non-empty.
action: ACPSession authenticates and retries the session open.
expected_result: It sends method "authenticate" with the single parameter methodId set to authMethods[0], the FIRST advertised method, with no user choice and no preference ordering. It then retries openSession exactly once. A non-RPCError, an RPCError without "auth" in its message, or an empty authMethods list all skip the retry and the error propagates out of start(). The substring match is on the message only, not on the error code.
side_effects: One authenticate request; a second session/new or session/load.
failure_cases: The authenticate request itself is `try await`, not `try?`: its failure propagates out of start() and the session never opens.
The retried openSession's failure propagates; there is no third attempt.
A provider whose unrelated error text happens to contain the letters "auth" (for example "author") triggers a spurious authenticate.
cancellation: Cancellation of the awaiting task surfaces as CancellationError from the pending request.
windows_path: Same. Use a case-insensitive indexOf on the message string; do not switch to a code check.
verification_method: contract fixture (scripted agent that rejects the first session/new with an auth message, then accepts)

title: baseModelID strips everything from the first opening bracket
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:432-436 - `guard let bracket = id.firstIndex(of: "[") else { return id }; return String(id[..<bracket])`; comment: Cursor's parameterized IDs are `model[effort=high,...]`; the picker stores the base name
